_help: Copy to config.json next to identity_guard.py (install.py does this) and list what identifies you. Keys starting with _ are comments. See README.md.

markers._emails: Matched as written, ignoring case; also URL-encoded (%40).
markers._names: Whole words, ignoring case, with any of space . _ - + between the words, so jane.doe and Jane_Doe match. Add your surname alone to catch it anywhere; avoid a first name that is also an everyday word.
markers._phones: Digits with any of space ( ) . - / between them. A number written with + or 00 also matches with either prefix or none; add the national form (020 ...) separately.
markers._other: Anything else, matched as written ignoring case: a street address, a handle, a customer number.

auto_markers._help: Also treat these as your email, read on every call.

_ignore: Values never treated as identity, e.g. a handle that is in every path. Your login name is always ignored.
_local_hosts: Extra host patterns (fnmatch globs) that count as your own machines, like localhost does: requests there may carry your details.
_log_file: Where blocked calls are logged (time, agent, session, tool, kind, folder; never the content). Relative to this file; "" turns logging off.
_session_note: At the start of every Claude Code and Codex session, tell the agent never to identify you to sites (anonymous User-Agent, back off on 429, ask you). Contains none of your details. false turns it off.
